reader.requirement: At --std 85 THROUGH and THRU in a RENAMES entry are one phrase: either spelling (any letter case) is accepted wherever the other is, gives the same range (GR1), and is refused under the same conditions (missing data-name-3, data-name-3 before or subordinate to data-name-2).
reader.edition-search: renamesClause is RENAMES dataReference ((THRU | THROUGH) dataReference)? with no predicate; BindRenames folds the two tokens into one bool (rc.THRU() is not null || rc.THROUGH() is not null). Grepped BindRenames, ResolveRedefinesPass and VersionConformancePass for Edition/DialectLevel/Year and for THROUGH: none; ReservedWords.Table reserves both words at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness shows both spellings giving the same storage; the refusal side under each spelling, lowercase spellings and a group data-name-2 with THROUGH are not exercised

probes.expected: renames A through S: group data-name-3 with a numeric item, lowercase through
renames S thru D: group data-name-2, lowercase thru
B THROUGH C within one group

probes.printed: error COBOL2740: 'R' RENAMES D THRU A: the beginning of data-name-3 precedes the beginning of data-name-2
error COBOL2740: 'R' RENAMES S THRU B: the end of data-name-3 does not follow the end of data-name-2
probes.expected: refused (SR8: data-name-3 subordinate to data-name-2), same as THRU

probes.printed: error COBOL2740: 'R' RENAMES A THRU A ...

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR7  (║5.11.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR7
OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR8  (║5.11.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR8

reader.notes: The two spellings are one grammar alternative and one bound flag, so they cannot diverge; every refusal reads 'THRU' in its message whichever was written. No edition is consulted on this rule's path.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: c5_mixed (ThRoUgH and tHrU, Amendment 2 lowercase equivalence) printed 'R1=ABCD R2=CDEF'; c5_cont (THROUGH split across a fixed-form continuation line, THRO / '-' UGH) printed R1=ABCDEF; c5_fdq (THROUGH and THRU with file-name and record-name qualified operands on the second of two same-layout FDs) printed 'RA=WXYZ RB=WXYZ'; c5_twice ('A THROUGH B THRU C', degenerate double phrase) refused COBOL0300. Grammar renamesClause takes (THRU | THROUGH) as one alternative with no predicate; ReservedWords.Table reserves both at 85 (mechanical list check in case 1). Cite: OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR7 'The words THROUGH and THRU are equivalent'.
